title: SLA-aware pacing controller for embeddings endpoint
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We've seen periodic tail-latency spikes on the embeddings endpoint during multi-tenant bursts. The existing autoscaler reacts on queue depth and GPU utilization but lacks fine-grained, SLA-aware pacing. This ticket proposes an SLA-aware pacing controller that dynamically shapes ingress per-tenant and per-route to meet p99 latency targets while smoothing bursts and minimizing overprovisioning.

Scope: Implement controller in the router layer that enforces token-based pacing budgets, bleeding capacity between tenants via soft-lease transfers, integrates with autoscaler signals, and emits telemetry for SLO compliance. Includes rollout plan, canary, and fallbacks to existing admission control.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change model quantization strategies or embedding model variants.
comments: 2026-02-12: Spike complete. Measured p99 tail latency contributors: enqueue jitter (40%), KV cache misses (30%), GPU preemption head-of-line (20%). Draft pacing algorithm uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/embeddings/pacing-spike

2026-02-18: Design review with infra and runtime teams. Agreed to keep pacing decisions stateless at router but delegated soft-lease bookkeeping to the provisioner service. Rafael to prototype token-bucket with gradient decay.
2026-02-25: Prototype shows 18% p99 reduction under synthetic burst and reduces GPU overprovision by 12% at 95th percentile load. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4682
2026-03-01: Security review flagged need for tenant-level telemetry scrub before logs leave VPC. Added telemetry scrub task and marked security_review_required true for follow-up (see dependencies).

2026-03-06: Load-test with multi-tenant flame graph attached in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/embeddings/loadtest/march-flamegraph.svg — tail latency improves, but one hot-tenant caused soft-lease starvation; mitigation: fair-share aging window introduced.
decisions: Keep pacing logic in the edge router for latency sensitivity; use provisioner for persistent quota bookkeeping.
Use hybrid token-bucket + leaky-window algorithm with per-tenant fairness weights and SLA multiplier.
Expose two config knobs per route: target_p99_ms and burst_headroom_ms. Default target_p99_ms = 150 ms for embeddings.
Fallback policy: when controller cannot allocate tokens within timeout, route request to lower-cost model variant instead of blocking.
acceptance_criteria: New pacing controller reduces p99 embedding latency by >=15% in production-like burst tests.
Autoscaler integrations prevent >30% overprovisioning compared to current baseline during 95th percentile bursts.
Observability: dashboards show per-tenant pacing utilization, denied requests, and SLA violations with alerts.
Rollout: Canary to 5% of traffic for one week with automated rollback on >2x SLA violations.
notes: Follow-up ticket required to integrate KMS-protected tenant identifiers in telemetry pipeline (security team). Monitor for edge token sync drift during clock skew.
